newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nokia sees sales in China up 50 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nokia sees sales in China up 50 pct in 1997.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications company Nokia Oy expects sales in China to reach 8.0 billion yuan (US$964 million) in 1997, up 50 percent from 1996, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Thursday.
Nokia announced the target at the first anniversary ceremony of its 70-percent-owned mobile phone venture in Dongguan city in southern China's Guangdong province, the newspaper said.
The Dongguan venture, set up in May 1995 with Guangdong Nanfang Communication Group at $25 million, has become one of Nokia's top mobile phone parts plants in the world, it said.
The venture is expected to have industrial output worth 800 million yuan in 1997, up from around 400 million yuan in 1996, it said.
"Today's celebration symbolises our confidence and commitment to China," the paper quoted a senior Nokia Asia-Pacific official as saying.
The newspaper gave no further details.
